children: Woodward plans to close a production facility in Santa Clarita, Calif., as part of its efforts to streamline its portfolio and manufacturing footprint.

The aircraft parts maker agreed to sell a group of legacy commercial rotorcraft, land systems and business jet products made in Santa Clarita, along with the campus itself. The sale is expected to close in fiscal year 2027.
Woodward said it will move production of military fixed-wing and rotorcraft flight control actuation from Santa Clarita to its campus in Spartanburg, S.C.
Woodward expects to cease operations at the California facility no later than December 2027. The decision is expected to affect about 400 roles.
In connection with the closing, Woodward expects to recognize pre-tax charges of $34 million to $47.5 million, due mainly to employee-related costs and contract terminations.

The Spartanburg campus is in advanced stages of construction and is set to go online in the summer of 2027. The site will produce Airbus A350 spoiler actuation systems in addition to the transferred product lines and other components.
